---
title: "Posterior profiles on multiple criteria"
subtitle: "4.1 · after the postrank vignette m2 and theory book, ch. 12"
description: "Criterion-specific scales, orderings and pairwise direction probabilities for common units."
---

The same units can rank differently across criteria, and each criterion carries its own pairwise direction probabilities. Compare posterior-mean orders and marginal intervals for any pair of sites.

```{=html}

```

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Thirty sites.** Across 435 pairs, 397 have opposing preferred directions, and a different site leads each criterion’s mean order.
- **Six sites, B–C.** Stating B above C has error .00666 on score A and .961 on score B, one of 3 opposing pairs.
- **Six sites, B–D.** Stating B above D has error .00234 on score A and .760 on score B under aligned unit labels.
- **Reverse score B.** Treating lower score B as higher priority reduces the B-above-C error on score B to .0385.
- **Wider intervals.** Raising marginal intervals to 95% widens uncertainty bands while keeping all 397 opposing pairs unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Marginal normal summaries and scope</summary>

In the six-site example, score A represents standardized reading growth and score B represents standardized family engagement, where higher scores ordinarily indicate earlier site visits without assigning funding. Each interval summarizes one marginal normal posterior; the thirty-site marginal release leaves cross-criterion joint draws and composite distributions undetermined.

</details>
